description: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services in India. It has replaced multiple indirect taxes, paving the way for a 'One Nation, One Tax' regime.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Understanding the fundamental principles of GST is crucial to grasp how it revolutionized the indirect tax structure in India.

key_concepts.explanation: GST is collected at the point of final consumption rather than the point of origin or production. The tax revenue goes to the state where the goods or services are finally consumed.
Also known as 'tax on tax', it occurs when a good is taxed at every stage of production without the benefit of a set-off. GST eliminated this by taxing only the value addition at each stage.
The backbone of the GST mechanism. It allows a business to reduce the tax they have already paid on inputs (purchases) from the tax they have to pay on their final output (sales).

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.description: The journey of GST in India spans over a decade, involving multiple committees and extensive legislative consensus.

historical_events.significance: This committee was the first to recommend a comprehensive Goods and Services Tax to reform the complex indirect tax structure in India.
GST was officially rolled out across India at midnight. July 1 is now celebrated annually as 'GST Day'.

important_facts.fact: France was the first country in the world to implement GST in the year 1954.
India's GST framework is a 'Dual GST' model, heavily inspired by the Canadian model, involving concurrent taxation by both the Center and the States.
Assam was the first state in India to ratify the GST Constitutional Amendment Bill.

sections.title: Constitutional Provisions
sections.description: Significant constitutional amendments were required to empower both the Center and the States to levy taxes concurrently on the same base.

polity_articles.provision: Amended the Constitution to introduce GST in India.
polity_articles.details: It was introduced in the Parliament as the 122nd Constitutional Amendment Bill.

polity_articles.provision: Special provision with respect to GST.
polity_articles.details: Grants concurrent power to both the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws regarding GST imposed by the Union or the State.

polity_articles.provision: Levy and collection of GST in the course of inter-state trade.
polity_articles.details: States that Integrated GST (IGST) on inter-state trade and commerce shall be levied and collected by the Government of India and apportioned between the Union and the States.
Empowers the President to constitute the GST Council within 60 days of the commencement of the 101st Amendment.

sections.title: Components and Tax Slabs
sections.description: Reflecting India's federal structure, GST comprises different components based on the nature of the transaction (intra-state vs. inter-state).

key_concepts.explanation: A tax levied by the Central Government on intra-state (within the same state) supply of goods and services.
A tax levied by the State Government (or Union Territory) on intra-state supply of goods and services.
A tax levied by the Central Government on all inter-state supplies (between two states) and on imports of goods and services into India.

important_facts.fact: There are four primary tax slabs under the GST regime: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%.
Essential items, including unpacked food grains, fresh vegetables, and unbranded milk, are kept under the 0% (exempted) slab.

sections.title: GST Council and Exemptions
sections.description: The GST Council is the apex governing body responsible for making recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, thresholds, and administrative procedures.

key_associations.extra_info: In the Council, the Central Government holds a 1/3rd voting weightage, while all State Governments combined hold a 2/3rd weightage. Decisions require a minimum 3/4th (75%) majority to pass.

key_associations.associated_with: Kept strictly outside the purview of GST
key_associations.extra_info: State governments continue to independently levy State Excise Duty and Value Added Tax (VAT) on alcohol, as it is a major source of state revenue.
Crude oil, motor spirit (petrol), high-speed diesel, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel will be brought under GST only from a date notified by the GST Council.
